verdicts.trueWording: Tyrion is an actual dwarf, a joke to passersby
verdicts.note: NPR live page fetched raw (HTTP 200, browser UA). Full sentence: "He is a dwarf, but he's not the gruff, hearty, axe-wielding hero of a noble dwarven race. He's not Gimli from The Lord of the Rings. Tyrion is an actual dwarf, a joke to passersby and an embarrassment to his family." Every limb (actual dwarf; joke to passers-by; not the hearty axe-wielding fantasy dwarf) is on the page. Page headline is 'G.R.R. Martin's Complex Epic For An Ambivalent Age', byline Lev Grossman, dated July 7, 2011 - matches the citation.

verdicts.trueWording: Martin is a tense, surging, insomnia-inflicting plotter
verdicts.note: content.time.com subscriber URL fetched raw (HTTP 200); full article text present, byline Lev Grossman, 'Books: The American Tolkien', Sunday, Nov. 13, 2005. Quote appears word for word.

verdicts.trueWording: and a deft and inexhaustible sketcher of personalities
verdicts.note: Same Time page, same sentence as index 526: '...is a tense, surging, insomnia-inflicting plotter and a deft and inexhaustible sketcher of personalities--including Tyrion Lannister...'. Verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: shoots the action from many angles, with a dozen narrators
verdicts.note: Time page: 'Martin shoots the action from many angles, with a dozen narrators, the better to reflect its gritty, twisty, many-sided nature and its vast cast...'. Both limbs (many angles / dozen narrators; to reflect its many-sided nature) supported verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: men and women slugging it out in the muck, for money and power and lust and love
verdicts.note: Time page closing lines: 'A Feast for Crows isn't pretty elves against gnarly orcs. It's men and women slugging it out in the muck, for money and power and lust and love.' The 'not elves against orcs' limb is the immediately preceding sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: Tolkien's work has enormous imaginative force, but you have to go elsewhere for moral complexity
verdicts.note: Time page: '...Tolkien's work has enormous imaginative force, but you have to go elsewhere for moral complexity. Martin's wars are multifaceted and ambiguous, as are the men and women who wage them...'. Both limbs verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: Tolkien was never quite so ponderous, and certainly not so obsessed with bodily functions
verdicts.note: Kirkus live page fetched raw (HTTP 200). Full text: 'Martin has been likened to J.R.R. Tolkien, but Tolkien was never quite so ponderous, and certainly not so obsessed with bodily functions of various sorts: "The Grand Maester befouled himself in dying, and the stink was so abominable that I thought I might choke."' All three limbs present, including the Grand Maester example.

verdicts.trueWording: a little cynical, plenty dark, few laughs, not much action, the usual blend of exposition
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'mostly exposition' - the page says 'the usual blend of exposition, sometimes seemingly endless, and the usual swords-and-sorcery dialogue', i.e. a blend of exposition AND dialogue, never that the book is mostly exposition
verdicts.note: Kirkus raw page carries the quote word for word: 'it's vintage Martin: It's a little cynical, plenty dark, with not many laughs and, truth be told, not much action.' The cynical / dark / few laughs / not much action limbs are all supported verbatim, and 'book five' matches ('The fifth installment'). Only the 'mostly exposition' limb overstates the page, which credits exposition as one half of a blend (albeit 'sometimes seemingly endless').

verdicts.trueWording: Jon Snow comes over all Hamlety, wondering what to do, soliciting input and then keeping his own counsel
verdicts.note: Kirkus raw page: 'out on The Wall the stalwart Jon Snow comes over all Hamlety, wondering what to do, soliciting input and then keeping his own counsel.' Quote and both trailing limbs verbatim. Only nuance: the page attributes this to Jon Snow the character rather than to 'Jon Snow's chapters' - an idiomatic difference, not a substantive one, in a review of a multi-POV novel.

verdicts.trueWording: on the evidence, one wonders if Martin isn't getting a little tired of it
verdicts.note: Kirkus raw page, closing verdict line: 'There's plenty of wiggle room for more volumes in the series, but on the evidence, one wonders if Martin isn't getting a little tired of it.' The 'on the evidence' limb and the referent 'it' = the Ice and Fire series are both on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: told through an array of constantly shifting perspectives
verdicts.note: Live washingtonpost.com refused the connection (curl: HTTP/2 stream not closed cleanly, INTERNAL_ERROR). Recovered via Wayback raw capture https://web.archive.org/web/20110713020646id_/http://www.washingtonpost.com/.../gIQAuJ1z9H_story.html (HTTP 200, 98 KB) - a raw page, not a summary. Text: 'The "Song of Ice and Fire" series is a hugely expansive narrative set in a variety of physical locales and told through an array of constantly shifting perspectives.' Both limbs (shifting perspectives; many locales) verbatim. Headline confirmed as "'A Dance with Dragons' worth the long long wait", byline Bill Sheehan.

verdicts.trueWording: vividly rendered set pieces, cliffhangers, appalling cruelty; epic fantasy as it should be written
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture: 'Filled with vividly rendered set pieces, unexpected turnings, assorted cliffhangers and moments of appalling cruelty, "A Dance With Dragons" is epic fantasy as it should be written: passionate, compelling, convincingly detailed and thoroughly imagined.' The cited quote is the appositive of that same sentence; every limb of the claim sits in it.

verdicts.trueWording: grounded in the brutal reality of medieval times; more in common with the Wars of the Roses
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture: 'the book - and the series as a whole - feels grounded in the brutal reality of medieval times and has more in common with the Wars of the Roses than it does with "The Lord of the Rings."' Quote verbatim and the Wars of the Roses / LOTR comparison is explicit.

verdicts.trueWording: as the characters repeatedly remind us, "Winter is coming"
verdicts.note: Same Wayback raw capture: 'As the narrative begins, a long, deceptively peaceful summer is coming to an end. And, as the characters repeatedly remind us, "Winter is coming."' Quote verbatim and the motto it attaches to is the claimed one.

verdicts.trueWording: as convincingly of tart juices oozing from an apple as of sleet on a mountain
verdicts.note: paullevinson.blogspot.com fetched live and raw (HTTP 200, 1.4 MB). Text: 'Martin writes as convincingly of tart juices oozing from an apple as of sleet on the side of a mountain, and his book is as much an adventure of the senses as it is of the mind.' Quote verbatim; both limbs supported. The page's own header line reads 'from Tangent Magazine, #16, Fall 1996', matching the citation (the blog post's slug says 'fall-2006', but the article header says 1996).
